findings.title: Decode captured timeout bytes before appending the drain marker
findings.trigger: A timed-out pytest process has emitted output, and a descendant in a separate process group retains its stdout pipe beyond DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.
findings.execution_path: _run_pytest calls run_command with text=True and stdout=PIPE. After the initial timeout, run_command kills the tracked group and retries communicate(). The drain timeout supplies bytes in drain_exc.stdout, which _with_drain_marker concatenates with a string at line 214.
findings.consequence: TypeError replaces the expected TimeoutExpired. _run_pytest cannot publish its partial test evidence or proceed to Codex; execute records a generic harness failure and aborts the review.
findings.evidence: The actual run_command reproduction printed "TypeError: can't concat str to bytes". Python's TimeoutExpired captured output remained bytes with text=True. test_post_kill_drain_is_bounded uses a child that emits nothing, so output is None and its assertion passes without exercising this failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize captured bytes using the subprocess encoding/error policy before appending a text marker, or preserve bytes consistently for the existing _run_pytest decoder. Extend the drain-timeout regression test to emit nonempty output and assert both preserved output and the marker on TimeoutExpired.
